outcome: Greene and Lobb (arXiv:2407.07798, 10 July 2024) proved an inscribed square exists for Jordan curves formed by two graphs with Lipschitz constant < 1+sqrt(2), a human-only case result. [Judged 2026-09-28; the researcher's original outcome follows.] The general inscribed square problem (does every Jordan curve have an inscribed square) remains open. Since 26 January 2024, genuine mathematical progress moved a case/bound (Greene and Lobb, July 2024, extended the Lipschitz-constant threshold under which a square is guaranteed to exist); separately, an independent researcher's November 2025 self-published claim of a full solution for C0 curves, produced in collaboration with AI systems (Gemini/ChatGPT), was subsequently acknowledged by its own author to contain an error and has not been fixed or accepted as of the most recent check.

ai.basis_quote: Ueoka used AI systems (ChatGPT and Gemini) for English drafting, translation, structured proof-checking, and detecting missing links in arguments, with Ueoka selecting and validating the final structure and mathematical content. ... An error was found in this proof, so we are considering an alternative approach.

summary: Two distinct threads occurred in the window, and neither settles the general problem, so status is `progress` rather than `resolved`, `claimed` or `partial`. (1) Genuine mathematics: Greene and Lobb, 'Square pegs between two graphs' (arXiv:2407.07798, submitted 10 July 2024), extended Tao's 2017 result to Jordan curves formed by two graphs with Lipschitz constant < 1+sqrt(2), a real bound-moving advance on a restricted case, with no AI involvement claimed anywhere in the paper. This is a case/bound within the window but, taken alone, would only warrant `partial`/`progress` with `ai_role` none; I folded it into one `progress` record with the more eventful AI incident as the dated event, per the instruction to describe multiple events in `summary` rather than open extra records. (2) The AI-linked item the triage flagged: independent researcher Yoshiki Ueoka published a Zenodo preprint (English: doi 10.5281/zenodo.18243635; also two Medium posts, Nov 2025 and a Jan 2026 follow-up) titled 'On the existence of squares inscribed in arbitrary C0 Jordan closed curves in the plane,' claiming to prove the fully general case via a topological-degree-theory argument, developed in collaboration with Gemini and ChatGPT. Critically, the Zenodo page itself carries the author's own caveat, fetched directly: 'An error was found in this proof, so we are considering an alternative approach. Once completed, we plan to submit it as a separate preprint.' So the claimed full resolution is a withdrawn/broken claim, not a standing one. On AI's role: per the author's own account (Zenodo metadata and Medium posts), the AI systems' contribution was English drafting/translation, structured proof-checking, and 'detecting missing links in arguments,' while Ueoka 'select[ed] and validat[ed] the final structure and mathematical content' — i.e., checking/proofreading/drafting, not producing the mathematics that ended up in the (broken) result. Under §6.2 that would ordinarily code as `none` (assistance limited to checking/proofreading/formalising), but because this is a claim that was announced and then itself invalidated by its author, I classified it under §6.1's 'instructive failure' clause as `progress` with `ai_role` `incident`, since the more load-bearing fact is that an AI-marketed claim was made publicly and collapsed, which is itself the kind of episode §6.2's `incident` code and §7's 'withdrawn claim is still an event' rule exist to capture. I also note Ueoka has a pattern of similarly self-published, AI-co-branded 'solutions' to other famous open problems (e.g. the Collatz conjecture), which is relevant context for weighing credibility but not dispositive on its own. I found no evidence any professional mathematician reviewed, endorsed, or even commented on the Ueoka claim; it has not been discussed on Tao's blog, in an arXiv listing, or in any digest I could locate. Wikipedia's own live article (checked via WebFetch on the current revision) still describes the general case as open, listing only pre-2024 partial results (Tao 2017, Chambers's 'close to C2' result). The Chambers paper the triage flagged (arXiv:2203.02613) was in fact first posted 4 March 2022 — well before the frozen revision — and its only in-window event is journal publication in Discrete & Computational Geometry (2025), which per §6.3 does not count as the dating event; I therefore treat it as `open_stale`-relevant background rather than an in-window advance, and it does not drive this record's status.
competing_reading: One could argue this record should be split, or that status should be `open` with `no_change_found` true on the grounds that the Ueoka claim is not a serious mathematical event at all (self-published, non-peer-reviewed, acknowledged-broken, by a non-specialist) and thus outside what should count as 'happened.' I judged that a publicly announced full-solution claim that named specific frontier AI systems as co-developers, went through two Medium posts and a Zenodo preprint, and was then retracted by its own author for an error, is exactly the kind of 'instructive failure' §6.1 and §7 ask to be recorded rather than dropped — dropping it would mean the record understates real AI-adjacent activity around this problem. A different reader might also argue `ai_role` should simply be `none` since the author's own description of AI's contribution (drafting, checking, translating) matches the `none` definition almost verbatim, and the 'incident' label overstates AI's causal role in the (broken) mathematics itself. I flag this tension rather than resolving it fully in one direction.
what_would_settle_it: A corrected version of Ueoka's preprint (or its retraction/silent abandonment) would settle whether this remains an open incident; and independent expert commentary (a blog post, MathOverflow thread, or citation) on the Ueoka claim would settle whether it merits any classification above 'incident'. For the Greene-Lobb thread, no further evidence is needed; it is settled as a genuine partial/bound advance with no AI role.

judgement.doubts: Greene–Lobb's result is a new class of curves (a case), not a bound on a quantity; one could read the Lipschitz threshold as a bound, which would give progress, but the settled object is a restriction of the question so case fits. 'incident' is not an allowed ai_role; the Ueoka AI use (drafting/checking) would be none anyway, and the claim is knocked down. Chambers is pre-snapshot and only a partial result, so it does not make the problem open_stale.
